b: For years I've struggled with brutal health anxiety, specifically around my heart and GI tract. But lately more about my heart, you know how it goes. It always moves around. Over the past couple of weeks I've been having weird random discomfort and chest pain, which prompted an urgent care trip last week where an EKG and X-ray came back totally fine. My PCP even scheduled a heart monitor and echo for early December just as a precaution to calm my nerves.

Well, today my Apple Watch popped up with an AFib detection. Seeing that notification completely sent me over the edge. I literally drove myself to the hospital while on the phone with 911. Hands down the worst panic attack of my life…
I’ve been sitting in this ER for the last 6 hours, and I'm finally back in my car.

They ran two EKGs, full blood work, and checked everything. The doc gave me a clean bill of health. He said nothing from today or the past week points to a heart attack, clots, or any actual problems, and that I look physically really strong and healthy. When I showed him my watch EKG, he wasn't sure what it actually caught, saying it could easily have been a harmless extra beat, a skipped beat, or just an artifact.

The first ER EKG had some artifacts whicu he said were harmless (which almost made me spiral all over again had he not said it was still fine) but the second one was super clean. The doctor also pointed out that if I'd had a heart attack or something in the recent times i’ve dealt with this (which come on, that’s what we all think is happening) , it would've showed up instantly in the labs as well.

I'm still gonna do the monitor and echo in December just because it's already scheduled and to officially check all the boxes, but the ER doc was totally unconcerned after taking my full history and running everything.

If you're out there dealing with health anxiety and feel like your brain is making up every physical symptom under the sun, you're not alone. Today was an absolute nightmare, but I survived
the gauntlet.

I feel like i could cry with relief but also some back up anxiety about it getting this bad again or what if the symptoms come back and i spiral but i will keep repeating the doctors words in my head that I am OK.
Heading home now to grab some Chipotle and finally try to relax.
